title: ProtonDrive Sync/Copy Never Ends
body: First off, I really appreciate the work done for ProtonDrive, its awesome !! #### What is the problem you are having with rclone? When running `rclone sync ./immich-data/ ProtonDrive:Backups/Photos/immich-data -P --transfers=10 --checkers=12 -vv` the command never ends. It works but after its done it just never stops and no debug logs. The 503 was from another rclone command I ran in the background. if I do a TCPDUMP command it shows communication happening to proton. #### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`) ``` ~ rclone --version rclone v1.65.0-beta.7369.af260921c - os/version: debian 12.1 (64 bit) - os/kernel: 6.1.0-10-amd64 (x86_64) - os/type: linux - os/arch: amd64 - go/version: go1.21.1 - go/linking: static - go/tags: none ``` #### Which cloud storage system are you using? (e.g. Google Drive) ProtonDrive #### How to use GitHub * Please use the 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to show that you are affected by the same issue. * Please don't comment if you have no relevant information to add. It's just extra noise for everyone subscribed to this issue. * Subscribe to receive notifications on status change and new comments.

Please don't send screenshots - they are impossible to work with! Paste the info into the issue or best of all, attach a log.

> The other think you could do is get it to the point where it appears locked up, then kill -QUIT it. This will produce a backtrace of exactly what rclone is doing. Post the backtrace here (as an attachment if large)

Please can you do this so we know where it is locked up.

You can collect the backtrace by running in a terminal with

    rclone ... 2>&1 | tee rclone.log

Then send the QUIT signal which is pressing CTRL-\ (or do `killall -QUIT rclone` from another terminal) when it locks up.

Please attach the log, or at very least edit it so it has the last few lines of the log and then the entire backtrace (which may be hundreds or thousands of lines long).

Thank you.

Hello @reporter, 

Thanks for reporting this performance issue. 

During my own testing, I did encounter issues when there are lots of files and folders being uploaded (such as if you are uploading `.git` folder), the performance will be slow. It's not hanging though, just that it's slow. 

Also, at some point the 429 error will happen since the current uploading mechanism might still be too aggresive to the Proton server, which I am also improving now!

I will shift my priority to address these issues as soon as possible! 

Cheers.

Henry

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> @participant3 could you explain in more detail how you got it running properly? In my case, rclone and Proton Drive is insanely slow...
I used `restic` to create a remote repo on my Proton Drive, then used `restic` to back up my files. Here's how I set this up:

1. create an `rclone` setup for `Proton Drive`; we'll use `proton` for this example.
2. create a remote `restic` repo: `restic init --repo rclone:proton:participant3`
3. run a backup (this backs up my entire $HOME): `restic backup /home/<user>/ --one-file-system --exclude-if-present .nosync --repo rclone:proton:participant3`

DM me if you have any other questions.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
I seem to be having a large issue with Proton Drive backups. For whatever reason if I'm syncing multiple files, progress will randomly be stalled as if the connection was lost, requiring a hard exit of rclone and a resync to resume progress.

My current solution is running an infinite loop with `timeout [5-10]m rclone [args]`. Obviously this should not be necessary, though.
